name: Familial Dysautonomia
aliases: Hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type III

prevalence.estimate: 1 per 3,600 live births in Ashkenazi Jewish population; extremely rare outside this group

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and genetic criteria for Familial Dysautonomia

criteria.description: Absence of fungiform papillae on the tongue
Depressed or absent deep tendon reflexes
Absence of axon flare after intradermal histamine injection
Miosis after conjunctival instillation of dilute methacholine (0.0625%)
Homozygous or compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in ELP1 (IKBKAP) gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation with biallelic pathogenic ELP1 variants; clinical features support diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: The major founder mutation (IVS20+6T>C) accounts for >99.5% of alleles in Ashkenazi Jewish patients.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Alacrima (absence of emotional tears) from birth
pathognomonic.notes: One of the earliest and most consistent findings

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent fungiform papillae on the tongue
pathognomonic.notes: Smooth tongue appearance is virtually pathognomonic

common.symptomName: Autonomic crises (episodic hypertension, tachycardia, diaphoresis, vomiting)
common.notes: Can be triggered by emotional or physical stress

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulty and dysphagia from infancy

rare.notes: Chronic kidney disease develops in some adults
May occur during autonomic crises with severe hypertension

laboratory: Genetic testing: ELP1 (IKBKAP) gene mutations (IVS20+6T>C founder mutation)
Plasma catecholamines: exaggerated norepinephrine/dopamine ratio during crises
imaging: MRI brain: may show optic nerve atrophy
genetic: Major Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutation: IVS20+6T>C (splice site)
other: Absent axon flare response to intradermal histamine
Pupillary supersensitivity to dilute methacholine (denervation supersensitivity)
Autonomic testing: severe cardiovagal, adrenergic, and sudomotor dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: HSAN II does not have autonomic crises
HSAN II has different genetic basis (various genes)
Familial dysautonomia has alacrima and absent fungiform papillae
CIP (HSAN IV/V) lack the prominent autonomic features of FD
CIP has different genetic basis (NTRK1, NGF mutations)

redFlags: Aspiration pneumonia (major cause of morbidity and mortality)
Severe autonomic crisis with BP >180/110 in a child
Corneal ulceration from absent corneal reflex
references: Axelrod FB. Familial dysautonomia. Muscle Nerve. 2004;29(3):352-363.
Norcliffe-Kaufmann L, et al. Familial dysautonomia: history, genotype, phenotype and translational research. Prog Neurobiol. 2017;152:131-148.
Palma JA, et al. Current treatments in familial dysautonomia. Expert Opin Pharmacother. 2014;15(18):2653-2671.
